rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: The LCM of the smallest prime number and the smallest odd composite number is :
rows.solution:
The smallest prime number is 2 and the smallest odd composite number is 9.

2 and 9 have no common factor, so their LCM is \(2 \times 9 = 18\), which is option (D) \(18\).

rows.stem: If the mean of the first n natural numbers is \(\dfrac{5n}{9}\), then the value of n is :
rows.solution:
The mean of the first n natural numbers is \(\dfrac{1 + 2 + \cdots + n}{n} = \dfrac{n(n + 1)}{2n} = \dfrac{n + 1}{2}\).

\(\dfrac{n + 1}{2} = \dfrac{5n}{9}\) gives \(9n + 9 = 10n\), so \(n = 9\). This is option (C) \(9\).

rows.subtopic: Trigonometric Ratios of an Acute Angle
rows.stem: If \(5\tan\theta - 12 = 0\), then the value of \(\sin\theta\) is :
rows.solution:
\(5\tan\theta - 12 = 0\) gives \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{12}{5}\). Take the opposite side 12 and the adjacent side 5; the hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{144 + 25} = 13\).

\(\sin\theta = \dfrac{12}{13}\), which is option (B) \(\dfrac{12}{13}\).

rows.stem: The \(14^{\text{th}}\) term from the end of the A.P. \(-11, -8, -5, \ldots, 49\) is :
rows.solution:
Here \(d = -8 - (-11) = 3\). Counting from the end, the A.P. runs \(49, 46, 43, \ldots\) with common difference \(-3\).

The \(14^{\text{th}}\) term from the end is \(49 + 13 \times (-3) = 49 - 39 = 10\), which is option (B) \(10\).

rows.stem: The length of the shadow of a tower on the plane ground is \(\sqrt{3}\) times the height of the tower. The angle of elevation of the Sun is :
rows.solution:
If the tower has height h, its shadow is \(\sqrt{3}h\), so \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}h} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) and \(\theta = 30^\circ\).

This is option (A) \(30^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: What is the probability that a number selected randomly from the numbers \(1, 2, 3, \ldots, 15\) is a multiple of 4 ?
rows.solution:
The multiples of 4 from 1 to 15 are 4, 8 and 12: 3 of the 15 numbers.

\(P = \dfrac{3}{15}\), which is option (C) \(\dfrac{3}{15}\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem:
The king, queen and ace of clubs and diamonds are removed from a deck of 52 playing cards and the remaining cards are shuffled. A card is randomly drawn from the remaining cards. Find the probability of getting

(i) a card of clubs.

(ii) a red coloured card.
rows.solution:
Six cards are removed (king, queen and ace of clubs and of diamonds), so \(52 - 6 = 46\) cards remain.

(i) The clubs left are \(13 - 3 = 10\), so \(P(\text{a card of clubs}) = \dfrac{10}{46} = \dfrac{5}{23}\).

(ii) The red cards left are the 13 hearts and \(13 - 3 = 10\) diamonds, 23 in all, so \(P(\text{a red card}) = \dfrac{23}{46} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

Write tan and cot in sines and cosines:

LHS \(= \dfrac{\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} - \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \dfrac{\sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}\)

\(= \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta} - \dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta} = \dfrac{1}{\cos^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\sin^2\theta}\)

\(= \sec^2\theta - \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta =\) RHS.

rows.stem: A sector is cut from a circle of radius 21 cm. The central angle of the sector is \(150^\circ\). Find the length of the arc of this sector and the area of the sector.
rows.solution:
Here \(r = 21\) cm and \(\theta = 150^\circ\).

Length of the arc \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r = \dfrac{150}{360} \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 21 = \dfrac{5}{12} \times 132 = 55\) cm.

Area of the sector \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi r^2 = \dfrac{150}{360} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 21 \times 21 = \dfrac{5}{12} \times 1386 = 577{\cdot}5\ \text{cm}^2\).

(The marking scheme prints the arc length as 55 cm\(^2\); a length is in cm.)

rows.stem: From a window 15 metres high above the ground in a street, the angles of elevation and depression of the top and the foot of another house on the opposite side of the street are \(30^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\) respectively. Find the height of the opposite house. (Use \(\sqrt{3} = 1{\cdot}732\))
rows.solution:
Let B be the window, with \(AB = 15\) m above the foot A, and let CD be the opposite house, with C its foot and D its top. Draw BP parallel to the ground, meeting CD at P, so ABPC is a rectangle: \(PC = AB = 15\) m and \(BP = AC = x\). The angle of elevation of D is \(\angle DBP = 30^\circ\) and the angle of depression of C is \(\angle PBC = 45^\circ\). Let \(DP = h\).

In right triangle BPC: \(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{PC}{BP}\), so \(1 = \dfrac{15}{x}\) and \(x = 15\) m.

In right triangle BPD: \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{DP}{BP}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{h}{15}\) and \(h = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{3}} = 5\sqrt{3}\) m.

Height of the opposite house \(CD = 15 + 5\sqrt{3} = 15 + 5 \times 1{\cdot}732 = 15 + 8{\cdot}66 = 23{\cdot}66\) m.

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A juice seller was serving his customers using glasses as shown in the figure. The inner diameter of the cylindrical glass was \(5{\cdot}6\) cm, but the bottom of the glass had a hemispherical raised portion which reduced the capacity of the glass. If the height of the glass was 10 cm, find the apparent capacity and the actual capacity of the glass.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - an open cylindrical glass whose base carries a raised hemisphere spanning the whole base; that the hemisphere's radius equals the glass's inner radius is shown only in the drawing, the stem gives the diameter and height of the glass alone. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
The radius of the glass is \(r = \dfrac{5{\cdot}6}{2} = 2{\cdot}8\) cm and its height is \(h = 10\) cm. The raised hemisphere at the bottom has the same radius, \(2{\cdot}8\) cm.

Apparent capacity \(= \pi r^2 h = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2{\cdot}8 \times 2{\cdot}8 \times 10 = 246{\cdot}4\ \text{cm}^3\).

Volume of the hemispherical portion \(= \dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2{\cdot}8 \times 2{\cdot}8 \times 2{\cdot}8 = 45{\cdot}99\ \text{cm}^3\) (to two decimal places).

Actual capacity \(= 246{\cdot}4 - 45{\cdot}99 = 200{\cdot}41\ \text{cm}^3\), about \(200{\cdot}4\ \text{cm}^3\).

(The marking scheme cuts the hemisphere's volume off at \(45{\cdot}9\ \text{cm}^3\) and so reaches \(200{\cdot}5\ \text{cm}^3\); carried to two places, the actual capacity is \(200{\cdot}41\ \text{cm}^3\).)

rows.stem: What is the median class of the above given data ?
rows.context:
Activities like running or cycling reduce stress and the risk of mental disorder like depression. Running helps build endurance. Children develop stronger bones and muscles and are less prone to gain weight. The physical education teacher of a school has decided to conduct an inter school running tournament in his school premises. The time taken by a group of students to run 100 m, was noted as follows :

| Time (in seconds) | 0 – 20 | 20 – 40 | 40 – 60 | 60 – 80 | 80 – 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of students | 8 | 10 | 13 | 6 | 3 |

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - an overhead photograph of sprinters at the start of a race on a running track; the data are in the table. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
| Time (in seconds) | 0-20 | 20-40 | 40-60 | 60-80 | 80-100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of students (f) | 8 | 10 | 13 | 6 | 3 |
| cf | 8 | 18 | 31 | 37 | 40 |

\(N = 40\) and \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 20\). The first cumulative frequency above 20 is 31, so the median class is 40-60.

rows.stem: Find the mode of the above given data.
rows.context:
Activities like running or cycling reduce stress and the risk of mental disorder like depression. Running helps build endurance. Children develop stronger bones and muscles and are less prone to gain weight. The physical education teacher of a school has decided to conduct an inter school running tournament in his school premises. The time taken by a group of students to run 100 m, was noted as follows :

| Time (in seconds) | 0 – 20 | 20 – 40 | 40 – 60 | 60 – 80 | 80 – 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of students | 8 | 10 | 13 | 6 | 3 |

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.solution:
The highest frequency is 13, so the modal class is 40-60, with \(l = 40\), \(f_1 = 13\), \(f_0 = 10\), \(f_2 = 6\), \(h = 20\).

Mode \(= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 40 + \dfrac{13 - 10}{26 - 10 - 6} \times 20 = 40 + \dfrac{3}{10} \times 20 = 46\) seconds.
